claim: agentic-stack-agent-blend.sh conflict playbook (v0.9.0->v0.18.0 cycle): (1) dead-duplicate-line conflicts (PT has a stale naive computation immediately overwritten by a corrected one, upstream has just the clean line) -> take upstream. (2) naive-timestamp-interpretation conflicts -> keep PT's local-time-and-convert version, not upstream's assume-already-UTC shortcut, because PT's own historical writers used bare datetime.now().isoformat() which captures local time. (3) two independent same-line fixes (e.g. PT's path-sanitizer wrapper + upstream's tz-awareness fix) -> combine both, never pick one side, since either fix alone reintroduces an already-solved bug. (4) pure mechanical refactors (context-manager wrap, line reorder) -> take upstream. (5) new content merged into an existing non-blocked file that itself references a blocklisted skill (e.g. skills/_index.md gaining a '## brain' section) -> union everything except the blocklisted reference; the tool's path-level blocklist does not scan merged file CONTENT for blocked references, only new file paths -- a known gap.

decisions.notes: Walked all 7 real conflicts from the first blend cycle with the user via AskUserQuestion on 2026-07-11; full detail in docs/wiki/11-agentic-stack-agent-blend.md. Recorded so the next agentic-stack pin bump doesn't re-derive these judgment calls from scratch.
